overview: This one-page file consists of a cross-reference sheet concerning the proposed use of Bank of Formosa capital to provide special loans to Japanese merchants, farmers, and industrialists in Malaya and the Netherlands Indies. It directs researchers to file 894.51/474 for an October 19, 1936 despatch from Hoover in Hong Kong to the Embassy, which transmitted an October 17 clipping from the South China Morning Post. The referenced despatch and clipping are not themselves present in this bundle.

subfiles.summary: This filing note directs the reader to file 894.51/474 for an October 19, 1936 despatch from Hoover in Hong Kong to the Embassy. The referenced despatch reportedly transmitted a South China Morning Post clipping dated October 17, 1936. Its subject was a Bank of Formosa plan to make special loans to Japanese merchants, farmers, and industrialists operating in Malaya and the Netherlands Indies.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence of State Department interest in Japanese and Formosan capital expansion into colonial Southeast Asia during the 1930s. Its distinction among merchants, farmers, and industrialists suggests a broad program of overseas economic penetration rather than an isolated commercial loan. It also preserves the archival relationship among diplomatic reporting, press evidence, and another decimal-file location, although the underlying despatch and clipping are absent here.
